importance.reason: A basic quantum transformation problem under black-box access, clarifying what an oracle interface permits.

sentences: An arbitrary unitary transformation may require an enormous circuit when described directly.
This question asks whether access to a suitably chosen classical Boolean oracle can always make that transformation efficiently implementable by a quantum computer.
The oracle may depend on the unitary, but the implementation must act correctly on arbitrary input states.
Aaronson's survey distinguishes this from preparing one chosen state or reproducing the unitary on only a few basis vectors.
The problem tests whether difficult quantum transformations can always be made easy by supplying enough classical black-box information.
